passages.title: The flight plan and the public interest
passages.text:
A new aviation rulebook was introduced after years in which civil aviation had relied on rules drafted for a very different industry. The update addressed aircraft registration, airworthiness, crew licensing, aerodrome operations and air navigation services. Operators welcomed clearer provisions, while safety advocates asked whether a more modern framework would still be enforced consistently. The regulator argued that a rulebook is only the first part of safety: inspections, training, reporting and independent investigation remain essential. The challenge was not simply to replace old language but to build a framework that could accommodate new aircraft technologies without weakening public confidence.
